chunks.citation: Shin, C et al. (2021). Anaerobic membrane bioreactor model for design and prediction of domestic wastewater treatment process performance. CHEM ENG J.
chunks.text: A pilot-scale system, consisting of a grit tank and microscreen for primary treatment followed by a SAF-MBR 2.0 for secondary treatment, was installed at the Codiga Resource Recovery Center (Stanford, CA), as illustrated in. The pilot-scale system treated municipal wastewater pumped from the Serra Street sewer on the Stanford campus for more than three years. Sewage was de-gritted in a grit tank then subject to primary treatment by screening through a 0.3 mm pore size microscreen (MS-28, Hydro International). The pilot-scale SAF-MBR 2.0 consisted of: (1) two AFBRs operated in parallel, hereafter referred to as AFBR 1 and AFBR 2, containing fluidized GAC biocarrier, and (2) a gas-sparged membrane tank equipped with ultrafiltration membranes. Recirculation of bulk fluid (twice the influent flow rate) between the three reactors enabled complete mixing and control of solids accumulation within the gas-sparged membrane tank.

chunks.text: Screens and grit removal are widely employed in WWTPs as they enhance the operation and maintenance of subsequent treatment units. Recent innovations in pretreatment technologies have brought the heavy cost of grit in WWTPs operations lower which has been considered an unavoidable burden. For example, based on advanced Grit Management™, Headcell® grit separation system was developed to achieve optimum grit removal for more than 30 years in the UK and USA. Headcell® is capable of achieving 95% removal of all grit 75 μm and larger. Because of its no-moving part design involving a hydraulically driven system, it delivers grit removal over a wide range of flows in a much smaller energy footprint than the conventional removal systems (Barter and Sherony, 2011) . chunks.citation: Zhou, N et al. (2019). Role of sludge retention time in mitigation of nitrous oxide emission from a pilot-scale oxidation ditch. BIORESOURCE TECHNOL.
chunks.text: A pilot-scale plexiglas Carrousel oxidation ditch was constructed, in which three semicircular channels were connected to four 1.15-m long straight channels. The ditch was 0.35-m wide and 0.5-m deep with a total working volume of 1.4 m 3 . Air was introduced from four 1-m long microporous aerator pipes located at the base of the second and third channels. The sketch of the reactor can be found in the supplementary information (SI). Experimental activated sludge was seeded from a steady-running SBR process in a municipal WWTP. The COD and NH 4 + -N concentration of synthetic wastewater were controlled at 250 mg L −1 and 50 mg L −1 , and pH was approximately 7.8 without adjustment. The liquor temperature was maintained at 22 ± 2 °C with a heating rod. Before getting into the inlet of the first channel, the influent and returned sludge were firstly pumped into a 50-L bioselector with continuous blending to avoid sludge bulking problem. The variations of HRT and SRT were achieved by altering the daily influent and sludge discharge rate.

chunks.citation: Thompson, M et al. (2022). Environmental Life Cycle Assessment of small water resource recovery facilities: Comparison of mechanical and lagoon systems. WATER RES.
chunks.text: Lagoons examined in the study exhibited several different configurations which are summarized in Fig. 1 . The configuration for complete retention lagoons is shown in Fig. 1b and only has water exiting the system via evaporation and seepage. Irrigation lagoons, shown in Fig. 1c , periodically pump treated water to local cropland for irrigation of crops. Controlled discharge facultative lagoons, shown in Fig. 1d , include periodic discharge of treated water to local water ways and may also include a UV disinfection system if discharging during the recreational session (i.e., May 1st -October 1st). For all lagoons, influent water is pumped to the site before proceeding through preliminary treatment and entering the lagoon cells where it is retained for extended periods of time. Water exits via evaporation or seepage through the liner, is completely retained (i.e., CR lagoon), intermittently discharged to a local water way (i.e., controlled discharge facultative lagoon), or pumped for land application to nearby agriculture land (i.e., irrigation lagoon).

chunks.text: Waste stabilization pond treatment systems (also known as lagoons) are another common type of biological wastewater treatment systems for small communities, as they account for more than 50% of the wastewater treatment facilities in the U.S. (US EPA, 2016) . Many different types of lagoons exist and may carry variations in terminology, common types include: controlled discharge (CD) lagoons, anaerobic lagoons, aerobic stabilization ponds, irrigation lagoons (Irrig), complete retention (CR) lagoons, and mechanically aerated oxidation ponds (Gloyna, 1971) . The mechanisms for treatment of wastewater are similar to that of AS process where bacteria are used for metabolizing organic waste; however, lagoons typically occupy a large land footprint area, have long detention times (5-180+ days), and utilize the natural convention of wind to provide oxygen to the water (Abdul et al., 2011) . Furthermore, many Lagoons facilitate the growth of algae that help assimilate nitrogen and phosphorous that in turn oxygenate the lagoon.

chunks.text: During the denitrification process, nitrate nitrogen (NO 3 -N) in the wastewater is reduced to nitrogen gas (N 2 ) under the action of denitrifying bacteria. Denitrification is a biochemical reaction carried out by heterotrophic microbes mainly that utilize the nitrogen from nitrates (NO 3 -N) as electron acceptors and carbon sources as electron donors under conditions of extremely low dissolved oxygen. Based on practical engineering applications, when the ratio of BOD 5 to TN in the wastewater entering the denitrification process is less than 4, the addition of external carbon sources should be considered. If the ratio c(BOD 5 )/c(TN) is 4 or higher, the process of denitrification can be considered complete (Fu et al., 2022; Sun et al., 2016) . In view of the strong acidity, a two-step approach was performed to treat chemical polishing wastewater. In step I which was carried out in one-chamber Fe-O 2 -FC, nearly all of Al 3+ was removed (~100%) and recovered in form of AlPO 4 (5.13 kg/t chemical polishing wastewater). Meanwhile, plenty of Fe 2+ was accumulated for the following PO 4 3− removal. In step II with pH being adjusted from 3.0 to 7.0, PO 4 3− precipitated with Fe 2+ to form vivianite. The total removal efficiency of PO 4

3− was 77.87%, and the vivianite yield was 13.22 kg/t chemical polishing wastewater. Except for vivianite, Fe(OH) 2 was the other sink of Fe 2+ in step II. Pollutants, i.e. COD and SS was coagulated by Fe(OH) 2 with removal efficiencies of 22.96% and 16.67%.
